sections.heading: Work done by a constant force

questions.q: A force of $40$ N pushes a crate a distance of $6$ meters along a horizontal floor, in the direction of motion. Find the work done.
A rope pulls a sled with a force of $80$ N at an angle of $30^\circ$ above the horizontal, moving it $10$ meters horizontally. Find the work done.
A force of $25$ N pulls a box a distance of $12$ meters along a horizontal floor, in the direction of motion. Find the work done.
Find the kinetic energy of a car of mass $1000$ kg traveling at $25$ m/s.
Find the kinetic energy of a cyclist and bicycle with combined mass $90$ kg traveling at $8$ m/s.
Find the kinetic energy of a ball of mass $0.2$ kg traveling at $15$ m/s.
Find the gravitational potential energy gained by a $60$ kg hiker climbing $150$ meters, using $g=9.8$ m/s$^2$.
Find the gravitational potential energy gained by a $5$ kg object lifted $12$ meters, using $g=9.8$ m/s$^2$.
Find the gravitational potential energy gained by a $15$ kg object lifted $8$ meters, using $g=9.8$ m/s$^2$.
A ball of mass $0.5$ kg is moving at $4$ m/s when a resultant force acts on it, increasing its speed to $10$ m/s. Find the work done on the ball, using the work-energy theorem.
A car of mass $900$ kg is moving at $20$ m/s when the brakes bring it to rest. Find the work done by the braking force, using the work-energy theorem.
questions.answer: $W=\Delta KE=0-\dfrac{1}{2}(900)(20^2)=0-180000=-180000$ J (negative, since the braking force removes kinetic energy).

questions.q: A skateboard and rider of mass $60$ kg is moving at $3$ m/s when a force accelerates them to $9$ m/s. Find the work done, using the work-energy theorem.
A ball of mass $2$ kg is released from rest at the top of a smooth (frictionless) ramp of height $5$ meters. Find its speed at the bottom, using conservation of energy and $g=9.8$ m/s$^2$.
A pendulum bob of mass $1$ kg swings from a height of $0.8$ meters above its lowest point. Find its speed at the lowest point, using $g=9.8$ m/s$^2$.
A skateboarder of mass $50$ kg starts from rest at the top of a smooth (frictionless) ramp of height $3.2$ meters. Find their speed at the bottom, using conservation of energy and $g=9.8$ m/s$^2$.

sections.heading: Energy loss due to friction or resistance

questions.q: A skier of mass $70$ kg slides down a slope, descending a height of $40$ meters. Their speed at the bottom is measured at $20$ m/s. Find the energy lost to friction and air resistance, using $g=9.8$ m/s$^2$.
A sled of mass $20$ kg slides down a slope, descending a height of $10$ meters. Its speed at the bottom is measured at $12$ m/s. Find the energy lost to friction, using $g=9.8$ m/s$^2$.
A crate of mass $30$ kg slides down a ramp, descending a height of $6$ meters. Its speed at the bottom is measured at $8$ m/s. Find the energy lost to friction, using $g=9.8$ m/s$^2$.
questions.answer: $PE$ lost $=mgh=30(9.8)(6)=1764$ J. $KE$ gained $=\dfrac{1}{2}(30)(8^2)=960$ J. Energy lost to friction $=1764-960=804$ J.

questions.q: A motor does $18000$ J of work in $12$ seconds. Find its power output.
A car engine produces a constant driving force of $2000$ N while traveling at a constant speed of $18$ m/s. Find the power output, using $P=Fv$.
A pump does $54000$ J of work in $45$ seconds. Find its power output.
A crane does $63000$ J of work in $70$ seconds. Find its power output.

sections.heading: A well-designed word problem: a cyclist climbing a hill

questions.q: This question has two parts. A cyclist and bicycle have a combined mass of $80$ kg. The cyclist rides up a hill, climbing a vertical height of $30$ meters over a time of $60$ seconds, starting and ending at the same speed of $6$ m/s (so kinetic energy does not change). Air and rolling resistance do a total of $900$ J of negative work against the cyclist during the climb. Use $g=9.8$ m/s$^2$. (a) Find the total work the cyclist must do against gravity and resistance combined. (b) Find the cyclist's average power output during the climb.
questions.answer: (a) Work against gravity: $mgh=80(9.8)(30)=23520$ J. Total work needed (gravity plus overcoming resistance): $23520+900=24420$ J. (b) Average power $=\dfrac{W}{t}=\dfrac{24420}{60}=407$ W.
